title: EQTransformer-based catalog reveals a 50-km-deep outer-rise fault at the Southern Mariana trench
summary: Applying EQTransformer phase detection to near-field ocean-bottom seismometer recordings collected near the Challenger Deep yielded more than 1,975 earthquakes. Relocation and waveform-similarity clustering outlined a southern Mariana outer-rise fault extending approximately 20–50 km below the seafloor (about 50 km maximum depth), inferred to be a reactivated normal fault; the depth suggests more incoming-plate water input than prior estimates.
organization: The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Qingdao National Laboratory for Marine Science and Technology; Southern University of Science and Technology; Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution

evidence.tested: Applying EQTransformer phase detection to near-field ocean-bottom seismometer recordings collected near the Challenger Deep yielded more than 1,975 earthquakes.
evidence.unknown: The fault depth, fault type and hydration implications are inferred from a localized seismic cluster, waveform similarity, and regional tomography; focal mechanisms could not be robustly resolved, and the authors state that limited station coverage does not establish whether such deep faults are widespread.
evidence.ai_role: Detected and picked P- and S-wave phases in near-field ocean-bottom seismometer data, producing a denser earthquake catalog. Researchers manually reviewed selected phases, relocated the events and used waveform-similarity clustering to delineate the fault.
